question: As recorded there is no shared question, because P-203's 91.1% is its AD vs CN accuracy. Once the record is corrected, both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion (pMCI vs sMCI) in ADNI from MRI: P-183 from T2-map signal and texture features plus neuropsychological scores, P-203 from whole-brain T1 sMRI with a 3D CNN. The horizons differ (2-year progressors against 5-year stables; conversion within 0-36 months against stability to 90 months), which the rule allows.
metric: After correction, accuracy with accuracy and AUC with AUC. As recorded, claim_a (72.7) is P-183's neuropsychology-only LASSO AUC, not an accuracy, and claim_b (91.1) is P-203's AD vs CN accuracy.

figures.P-183: Imaging plus neuropsychology, n = 40 (18/22): BSWiMS and RF accuracy 0.775 (printed 95% CI 0.615-0.892). ENS AUC 0.824 (0.681-0.968). BSWiMS balanced error 0.223 (0.100-0.359), i.e. balanced accuracy 0.777 (0.641-0.900).
figures.P-203: pMCI vs sMCI, trained on ADNI-1 and tested on ADNI-2 (75 pMCI/241 sMCI): accuracy 0.801, sensitivity 0.520, specificity 0.856, AUC 0.789. Wilson with n = 316: z^2/n = 0.0122, centre 0.797, half-width 0.044 -> 0.753-0.841. Hanley-McNeil with 75/241: Q1 = 0.789/1.211 = 0.652, Q2 = 2(0.6225)/1.789 = 0.696, SE = sqrt([0.1665 + 74(0.0290) + 240(0.0735)]/18075) = 0.033 -> 0.724-0.854. Balanced accuracy (0.520 + 0.856)/2 = 0.688. The printed sensitivity and specificity at 75/241 imply an accuracy of 0.776, not 0.801; either value gives the same verdict.
figures.comparison: 0.801 lies inside P-183's 0.615-0.892, and 0.775 lies inside P-203's 0.753-0.841. 0.789 lies inside 0.681-0.968, and 0.824 inside 0.724-0.854. The balanced accuracy of 0.688 lies inside 0.641-0.900. No metric excludes in either direction.

matched_figure_check: No reconciliation is needed beyond condition 4, because the corrected conversion figures agree. P-203's AD vs CN 91.1% has no counterpart: P-183 contains no AD vs CN analysis.
performance_validity: Passes: no compared figure reaches 0.97. P-203's AD vs CN AUC of 0.950 is below the threshold and is not a compared figure.
reason: The recorded disagreement exists only through two misreadings. P-203's 91.1% is AD vs CN, and P-183's 72.7 is an AUC from its neuropsychology-only model (condition 6). On the conversion figures both papers print, P-183's 0.775 and P-203's 0.801 each lie inside the other's interval, and so do the AUCs (0.824 and 0.789), so condition 4 fails.

quotes.quote: our model achieves accuracy values of 91.1 and 80.1% on ADNI-1 for AD diagnosis and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) convention prediction, respectively.
Progressive MCI (pMCI): Subjects are diagnosed with MCI who would gradually progress to AD within 0–36 months.
The ADNI-2 dataset has 643 3T T1W sMR brain images, including 143 AD, 184 CN, 75 pMCI, and 241 sMCI.
The machine learning technique with the best results was LASSO, with an accuracy of 0.675 and an ROC AUC of 0.727.
